info.title: API.SH: NFL
info.description: The NFL API from API.SH: public NFL data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.summary: NFL injury report for a week
get.description:
The official injury report of a week, team by team for each game: players with position, injuries, practice participation and game status (Out, Doubtful, Questionable). Filter by `team`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-injuries

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: Season year (the season that starts that September), e.g. 2026; the current season by default.

parameters.name: season_type
parameters.description: `PRE` (preseason), `REG` (regular season) or `POST` (playoffs); the current one by default.

parameters.name: week
parameters.description: Week number (regular season 1-18); the current week by default.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: Team abbreviation, e.g. `KC`, `SF`, `PHI`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A player's profile: name, position, jersey, team, roster status, height, weight, arm and hand length, experience, college, age, birth date, hometown, headshot and the recent-games stats table shown on the profile.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-player

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Player slug as in the nfl.com link (`patrick-mahomes`) or the link itself.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: NFL player statistics (season, career, game logs, splits)
get.description:
A player's statistics tables as nfl.com shows them: `summary` (recent games and season by season), `career` (every season and career totals per stat group), `logs` (game-by-game for a season), `splits` and `situational`. Each table has a `title`, `columns` and `rows`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-player-stats

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Player slug as in the nfl.com link (`patrick-mahomes`) or the link itself.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: `summary` (default), `career`, `logs`, `splits` or `situational`.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: Season for `logs`, `splits` or `situational`; the latest by default.

parameters.name: season_type
parameters.description: With `season`: `REG`, `POST` or `PRE`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A team's roster for a season: each player's `id`, `gsis_id`, `name`, jersey, position and position group, roster status (ACT, RES, PUP ...), height in inches, weight in pounds, birth date, NFL experience, colleges and headshot.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-roster

parameters.name: season

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: NFL schedule and scores for a week
get.description:
Every game of one week (the current week by default): `id`, `slug`, `url`, date and kickoff time, `status`, `phase` (FINAL, INGAME ...), quarter and clock, both teams with score, score by quarter and timeouts, venue, TV and streaming networks, attendance, weather, down and distance while live, the game book link and ticket link. `bye_teams` lists the teams on a bye in the current week. Filter by `team`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-schedule

get.description:
Season player statistics for one category, sorted like nfl.com's stats pages: each player's `name`, `slug`, `url` and every column of the table in `stats` (e.g. passing yards, yards per attempt, completions, touchdowns, interceptions, rating, sacks). `sort_keys` lists the sortable columns and their keys. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-stats-players

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Stat category.

parameters.name: season
parameters.description: Season year (the season that starts that September), e.g. 2026; the current season by default.

parameters.name: season_type
parameters.description: `REG` (default), `POST` or `PRE`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: A sort key from `sort_keys` (e.g. `passingtouchdowns`); the category's main stat by default.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `desc` (default) or `asc`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/nfl-stats-teams

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: `offense` (default), `defense` or `special-teams`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Offense: passing, rushing, receiving, scoring, downs. Defense: passing, rushing, receiving, scoring, tackles, downs, fumbles, interceptions. Special teams: field-goals, scoring, kickoffs, kickoff-returns, punts, punt-returns.

parameters.name: season

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
